course_name: Analysis and Processing of Time Series

course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A comprehensive course on time series analysis methodologies and technologies, spanning from classical statistical methods to modern deep learning implementations.
course_profile.short_summary: This course provides in-depth competencies in processing sequential data, building upon foundational Data Science concepts. Students learn to prepare temporal data and apply diverse forecasting and analysis techniques, including ARIMA models, Kalman filtering, and artificial neural networks using Python, TensorFlow, and PyTorch. The curriculum heavily emphasizes practical application in domains like economics, digital twins, and automated systems.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the mathematical models and properties of random processes.
Comprehend the theory behind statistical learning methods like Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and nonlinear models.
Understand how artificial neural networks are conceptualized and applied to sequential data.
practical_implementation: Implement robust data preparation pipelines handling parsing, missing values, anomalies, and normalization.
Develop and train statistical models including ARMA, ARIMA, and exponential smoothing using Python.
Construct deep learning architectures for time series using TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch.
analysis_validation: Conduct time series decomposition, correlation analysis, and clustering to derive insights.
Evaluate forecasting models and perform multifactor scoring.
architecture_design: Design analytical solutions capable of forecasting hierarchical and grouped time series data.
Integrate multiple Python libraries (Numpy, Pandas, Scipy, Scikit-learn) into cohesive data processing pipelines.
research_and_prototyping: Execute R&D projects predicting economic indicators, currency market changes, and behaviors of automated/unmanned systems.

what_student_can_understand: The underlying statistical properties of time series and how random processes behave.
The theoretical mechanisms of classical models like moving averages, Kalman filters, and ARIMA.
How different neural network frameworks (PyTorch vs TensorFlow) manage sequential temporal data.
what_student_can_build: Complete data preprocessing pipelines in Python using Pandas and Numpy.
Predictive statistical models using Scikit-learn and Scipy.
Custom neural network forecasting models trained on domain-specific historical data.
what_student_can_apply: Time series analysis to real-world problems like currency market prediction, automated system control, and economic indicator forecasting.
